description: Illustrative risk-based starting set, not a certification, exhaustive inventory, or universal priority assignment. Source checklist text remains authoritative.

priority_definitions.P0: Potential release blocker when applicable and unmitigated; human approval required for exceptions.
priority_definitions.P1: Important verification; investigate gaps and track resolution or approved exceptions.
priority_definitions.P2: Supporting assurance or context; apply when risk and architecture warrant it.

checks.criterion: Assets, sensitive data, trust boundaries, external dependencies, and data flows are inventoried.
A threat model covers realistic attacker goals, entry points, misuse cases, and mitigation owners.
Least privilege, role separation, service-account scopes, and periodic access reviews are applied.
Validate untrusted inputs against explicit server-side contracts at applicable trust boundaries.
Secrets are centrally managed, rotated when necessary, and scoped to their purpose.
Logs, traces, analytics, and error reports exclude secrets and unnecessary personal data.
Critical user journeys, business rules, edge cases, and negative cases are identified and prioritized by risk.
Critical journeys are retested after fixes; regression suites pass.
Known defects are triaged by severity; no unaccepted release-blocking defect remains.
Maintain a single release plan linking the source revision, immutable artifact, change summary, owners, milestones, and evidence locations.
Set measurable thresholds for error rates, latency, availability, transaction failures, and business guardrails that halt rollout.
Document tested rollback, traffic reversal, feature-disablement, and forward-fix options appropriate to the changed components.
Identify the applicable accessibility standards, legal/contractual obligations, and target conformance level with qualified reviewers when needed.
Verify tab order follows the intended interaction and does not produce confusing jumps or inaccessible controls.
Evaluate critical journeys with screen readers and supported browser/operating-system combinations.
Test forms for programmatic labels, descriptions, required fields, error association, and recovery after failed submission.
Ensure keyboard-only users can operate all essential functions without focus traps or undiscoverable commands.
Announce asynchronous status changes through appropriate live regions or other accessible notification patterns without over-announcing.
Ensure pointer targets, drag interactions, gestures, and hover/focus revealed content have accessible alternatives where required.
Check that destructive, privileged, or irreversible actions are not confused with routine navigation.
Show loading, empty, offline, unavailable, and error states that explain the condition and next step.
Use undo, edit, cancel, or confirmation patterns proportionate to the impact and reversibility of an action.
Check that client and server validation disagree neither silently nor through contradictory user messages.
Check CSRF protection for cookie-authenticated state-changing actions and other applicable request forgery risks.
Authorization is enforced server-side on every protected object, action, and tenant boundary.

Scan current source, available Git history/branches, build artifacts, and logs for passwords, API keys, private keys, or tokens; revoke or rotate confirmed exposures and assess impact instead of assuming removal from the latest commit resolves a leak.
Test tenant isolation at query, storage, cache, and API response boundaries.
Perform object-level authorization tests for manipulated IDs on every read, write, and delete endpoint (OWASP API1).
Test authentication token issuance, expiry, audience/issuer, signature validation, revocation, and replay resistance where relevant.
Enforce and test resource limits: rate, page size, payload size, timeouts, concurrency, and costly downstream calls (API4).
Test SSRF controls for URL-fetching endpoints and all outbound destinations (API7).
Validate implemented methods, routes, events, and message types against the published contract.
Test object-, function-, and property-level authorization, including tenant isolation.
Test repeated mutations and concurrent requests for idempotency and data integrity.
Test migrations against representative data volumes, versions, constraints, indexes, and realistic schema history.

Demonstrate point-in-time recovery to a selected timestamp or log position using a valid base backup and complete incremental/log chain; reconcile recovered business records with the agreed recovery objective.
Enforce object-, tenant-, account-, and operation-level authorization in the tool implementation regardless of the model's instructions.
Test prompt injection that tries to call higher-privilege tools, reveal secrets, or redirect the original user goal.
Do not treat tool descriptions, system prompts, output filters, or human-friendly warnings as substitutes for enforceable access controls.
Ensure cancellation propagates to pending model calls, queued tool work, child agents, and other resources where feasible.
Use operation identifiers and deduplication when retries or resumed workflows could replay non-idempotent tool calls.
Bind each approval to a specific run, pending tool call, immutable argument set, and authorized decision maker.
Revalidate current permissions and action arguments immediately before executing a previously approved tool call.
Provide a tested emergency stop that disables agent execution and revokes tools or credentials as appropriate.
Test retrieval isolation against users with similar queries but different document permissions.
Use controlled adversarial cases to verify malicious document text cannot change search permissions or trigger external actions.
Classify the system by potential impact and likelihood of harm using a documented, project-appropriate risk methodology.
Set explicit acceptance thresholds, review rules, and responsible approvers for high-impact outcomes.
Enforce user, tenant, role, scope, resource, and destination permissions in trusted execution code for every consequential tool call.
Record significant findings with owners, severity, mitigation, user impact, and validated retest evidence in project-specific records.
